description:
FDB has no deferred-metadata hold/confirm protocol because it never needs one: transactions touching \xFF are sent to ALL resolvers (CommitProxyServer.actor.cpp:2823 "\xff key space is processed by all resolvers"), so each resolver's local commit verdict for a state transaction IS the global verdict (Resolver.actor.cpp:397-400, StateTransactionRef committed flag from the resolver's own reply.committed). Bedrock's bedrock-q67.20.5 (PR #151, port of q67.17) instead defers accumulation: holds cap windows, proxies re-send globally-filtered confirms until acked, unconfirmed holds expire into the coverage-gap fail-fast. Correct and audited, but an entire protocol layer FDB's design makes unnecessary.

Evaluate adopting the FDB approach: route any transaction with \xFF-range write conflicts (and its metadata mutations) to every resolver, so accumulation can be immediate in sharded mode too, then DELETE hold/confirm (held_metadata_versions, settled_version, insert_sorted confirms, deferred_metadata re-send, expiry-into-pruned-floor, min-to window merging - most of PR #151). Cost: every resolver resolves system transactions (rare: recovery + future Distributor coverage writes) and their conflict ranges join every resolver's window. Touches conflict_sharding.ex routing; intersects bedrock-rag (system-range ingress validation). Decide AFTER the q67.20 stack lands and before/while q67.21 makes system-key writes routine - if adopted, it simplifies exactly the path the Distributor will exercise.

comments.text: FDB design audit: mechanism CONFIRMED, mapping REFINED, and the recorded 'only works for system-only-conflict transactions' constraint REFUTED with code - state txs carry unrestricted conflict ranges routed per-shard like any other (CommitProxyServer.actor.cpp:152-217); each resolver conflict-checks only ITS slice (Resolver.actor.cpp:338-359) and records StateTransactionRef(local_verdict, mutations) (:394-401, mutations only at resolver 0); the consuming proxy ANDs verdicts across all resolvers (applyMetadataEffect :1638-1642, alignment asserted :1212-1218). AND of per-slice verdicts IS the exact global verdict: every range is checked by its owner, system histories agree everywhere, non-owners yield trivially-commit. REFINED BEDROCK DESIGN: (a) do NOT broadcast conflict sections - keep sharding as-is; (b) send metadata_per_tx to ALL resolvers in sharded calls; accumulator entries become {version, [{mutations, local_verdict}]} INCLUDING verdict-false entries (absence != veto); (c) merge_metadata_windows: per-(version, tx_index) AND replaces dedup-by-version; window alignment holds (no holds -> settled==last; to_version uniform; ack-driven pruning can never prune a version still in another resolver's window); (d) own-batch metadata applied synchronously from the batch's own merged abort set - full apply (metadata+routing), ack honestly advances to commit version, FDB's applyMetadataToCommittedTransactions split; (e) DELETE: held_metadata_versions, settled_version, withhold_unsettled, apply_metadata_confirms, hold-expiry, insert_sorted, {hold?, confirms} protocol directives, proxy deferred_metadata + confirm re-send. PREREQUISITE (separate PR first): resolver stale-version retry clause (resolver/server.ex:179-194) FABRICATES an all-aborted reply; under verdict relay a lost-then-retried batch would leave commit-verdict entries in windows while clients hear aborted (today: bounded, chain-stall into recovery). Adopt FDB's outstandingBatches reply-replay cache per (proxy, version) (Resolver.actor.cpp:50, :330, :528-537). Phantom-metadata safety argument = version chaining at logs + epoch death, same as FDB.

Implemented as commits three and four of the follow-up stack: (1) q67.22-retry-replay - recent_replies cache replays recorded abort sets on retry, {:error, :version_beyond_retention} on cache miss, pruned with the retention sweep; (2) q67.22-converged-verdicts - hold/confirm deleted wholesale per the FDB design audit: metadata_per_tx broadcast to all resolvers, accumulator entries carry {mutations, local_verdict} (vetoes explicit), proxy merge ANDs verdicts positionally (raise on divergence), committed_window drops vetoed mutations before the serialized apply, windows cover the batch's own version so the deferred/own-entry path on the proxy is gone and the ack advances honestly to the commit version. Net -313 lines for the converged-verdict commit alone. Key correctness pin retained: 'metadata from a transaction aborted by only ONE shard resolver is never distributed' passes unchanged against the new protocol. Awaiting stack cold audit.

title: Evaluate replacing hold/confirm with FDB's broadcast-system-transactions-to-all-resolvers
